LLM_description:
Situation:
The division is executing sustained operations in contested terrain. Forward Operating Base Alpha (3rd Infantry Battalion), Combat Outpost Ridge (11th Armored Cavalry Squadron), and Fire Base Orion (Artillery Battery Echo) require continuous resupply of critical materiel. Multiple sources—including Supply Depot Bravo, Depot Charlie, Depot Delta, Depot Echo, Depot Foxtrot, Depot Golf, and Depot Hotel—hold stocks but are separated from supported units by exposed road networks. Primary movement corridors pass through a valley with intermittent indirect fire and IED activity; alternate ridge routes are narrow, weather-sensitive, and require engineer support for clearance. Movement control teams report periodic choke points at river crossings and culvert repairs. Air assets are limited and prioritized elsewhere; ground convoy is the primary method.

Mission:
Deploy ground convoys to deliver required supplies from available depots to supported units across the planning horizon, minimizing total operational cost while maintaining force protection and readiness. Costs include transport expenditures, shortage penalties for unmet demands, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Prioritize ammunition resupply to maintain combat power at FOB Alpha and Fire Base Orion; maintain sufficient sustainment for the cavalry squadron at COP Ridge.
- Allocate flows from each depot to units by day, constrained by depot on-hand capacities and route availability. Any shortfall is treated as temporary shortage and penalized; the objective is to minimize cumulative penalties.
- Enforce vehicle capacity using supply volume per unit moved. Convoy tasking cannot exceed fleet limits per day. Consolidate loads to reduce the number of activated routes when feasible.
- Route activation: opening a route on any day (sending any vehicles) triggers a fixed Risk Cost for that route-day, representing security overhead (escort teams, EOD/route clearance, EW overwatch, and UAV coverage), regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route.
- Movement control will avoid high-risk segments where costs outweigh operational benefit, favoring routes with acceptable transport and risk cost trade-offs. Engineer assets will be scheduled on activated routes only; non-activated routes will not receive clearance or escort.
- Commanders will review daily allocations to ensure demands are met within depot constraints while staying inside fleet limits. If risk and transport costs exceed acceptable thresholds, limited shortages may be accepted subject to penalty costs.
